newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products - Gasoline firms in U.S. Gulf.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products - Gasoline firms in U.S. Gulf.

text.p: Gasoline differentials shook off their early week slump in the U.S. Gulf Tuesday as heightened prompt demand had players buying conventional unleaded gasoline already loaded into the Colonial Pipeline.
New York Harbor reformulated gasoline weakened as midcontinent refiner Koch Industries was seen offering barrels in an already amply supplied market.
Meanwhile, unleaded gasoline was bid higher in the Midcontinent, but values were largely unchanged in quiet dealings.
NYMEX July gasoline was up 0.55 cent at 56.75 cent a gallon while NYMEX heating oil was up 0.40 cent at 51.90 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF

Conventional unleaded gasoline firmed in the U.S. Gulf as as players about conventional unleaded on the Colonial Pipeline en route to the New York Harbor, signalling higher demand for the region's tightly balanced supply.

"We had some buyers of front 17th (shipping cycle) M1 which spilled onto the back 17th. Supply is still in tight balance in the (U.S.) Gulf," said a dealer. The gasoline on the front 17th shipping cycle was loaded for shipping late last week.
Conventional unleaded was offered at 1.25 cents under NYMEX July gasoline after being offered at 1.50 cents under late Monday.
Premium unleaded 93 grade strengthened on the back of M1, with bids at 5.00 cents over NYMEX July gasoline compared with bids at 4.75 cents over late Monday.
The bid/ask spread for prompt heating oil tightened to 2.25 and 2.15 cents under NYMEX July heating oil respectively from a 2.30 and 2.05 cent spread on Monday.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Reformulated gasoline (RFG) differentials fell in the Harbor as barrels were being offered by a refiner, adding to supply there yet again.
"Koch was offering barrels earlier today, so the offers will be about 0.20 cents over when the dust settles," said a dealer.
RFG was offered at 0.30 cents over July NYMEX gasoline Monday. Unleaded conventional was unchanged at its offer of 2.25 cents under.
Sun Co posted a prompt heating oil price of 0.25 cent under July NYMEX heat, but dealers said the posting was below the market talk which offered heat at 0.15 cent under, in line with Monday.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent markets were quiet on Tuesday and largely unchanged. A refiner was heard buying Group Three unleaded gasoline at 6.00 cents over the July NYMEX, a quarter cent up from Monday. The deal, however, could not be confirmed.
Meanwhile, the Williams Pipeline Company on Tuesday forecast a decline in unleaded gasoline volumes, from 5.5 million barrels today to 4.5 million by June 23.

Williams officials reckoned the fall off in volume may be caused by refinery inventory problems at other points in the Williams system since the start of the pipeline at Tulsa, Oklahoma loaded at capacity.
-- New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1620
